### Added

- **Every shared display can be re-detected**: settings → Displays now has a re-detect button on each shared display's row. It reads the display again: which inputs it accepts, and which one it is showing. Until now that list was read once and never re-read, so a changed cable, a changed hub, or a first reading taken while the display was showing another computer left the list — and every input menu built from it — wrong indefinitely. What is stored is kept when nothing can be read, because a display that cannot be read is usually just a display showing somebody else.
- **An Experimental tab**: settings has a new section in the sidebar. Maintenance actions that write to a display, and have not been verified on enough hardware, appear only once they are turned on there. The choice is kept on this computer and is not shared with paired hosts.
- **Re-seat signal (experimental)**: when the picture does not arrive on an input that is already correct, this sends the display out through a paired host's input and straight back, so the link to this computer is re-established. A display's built-in USB hub or KVM binds itself to the active input rather than to the panel, so the keyboard and mouse come back with it.

  The return is the hard part. A display answers DDC/CI on the input it is showing and no other, so the moment the picture leaves this computer, this computer can no longer write to that display — the return has to be made by the host that is on screen by then. So the other host is asked to answer before the display is sent anywhere, and nothing moves if it does not. Coming back is not judged by whether a write reported success either: only a clean reading of the display counts. When it truly cannot be brought back, the message names which host's input the display stopped on and the two ways back: the display's own buttons, or MuxSU on that computer.

### Fixed

- **Windows DDC/CI calls never retried**: the macOS path always has; the Windows path never did. A display that has just changed input answers with malformed packets for a few seconds, which Windows reports as `ERROR_GRAPHICS_DDCCI_INVALID_MESSAGE_COMMAND` — and since a switch begins by reading the current input, that one failed read aborted the whole switch even when the write that followed would have worked. Windows reads, capabilities and writes now retry three times at 120 ms, matching macOS.

This version speaks the same protocol as v0.8.1 and pairs and switches with it directly.

### Known limitations

- Re-seat signal needs another paired host that answers right now and sits on a different input of the same display. That host is the picture's only way back, so the button stays disabled without one.
- Whether a display can be directed over DDC/CI is entirely up to its firmware, and what a display declares about its own support is not reliable. Re-seating has been verified on limited hardware, which is why it sits behind Experimental.
- The macOS DMG is ad-hoc signed and not notarized with an Apple Developer ID, so Gatekeeper may ask for it to be allowed by hand.
